correctness.rationale: Hypotheses include all m_i>=5 and flat squares. Explicit vertex switching puts signs on seams; nontrivial holonomies yield a signed double cover P/K of an unsigned doubled-coordinate product. The square-faithful covering lemma reconstructs GLMY allowed-boundary constraints, so ordinary homology of P/K equals K-invariant homology. Ordinary Cartesian path Künneth and long-cycle H0,H1 show every coordinate half-turn acts trivially, forcing the sign anti-invariant of the residual deck map to vanish for all p. When all holonomies are positive, ordinary binomial ranks follow. The published full texts support each imported theorem. The standalone checker tests 22 cubical and 12 direct low-degree signed GLMY cases; no finite computation is used to prove the universal conclusion.

value.rationale: The September 2026 signed path homology framework has sign-sensitive low-degree examples, but there is a natural open structural question for flat high-dimensional product test graphs. This theorem classifies all flat signings on arbitrary products of long cycles, showing a sharp dichotomy between binomial homology and complete acyclicity in every degree. It demonstrates a topology-relevant holonomy obstruction and establishes a reusable nonstandard path-chain descent mechanism rather than a mere numerical evaluation.
